nodes.title: Character Replacement Guide
widgets_values:
1. This continuation example is scene-specific, not a universal workflow.
2. Use the character-replacement skill to inspect new footage, plan segments and update each segment prompt and frame settings.
3. Configure Global Control, review segment previews, then assemble. Current frame settings assume 24 FPS.

widgets_values_named.text:
1. Enable the case you want to run; mute the others.
2. Replace its character images and source video(s).
3. Update the prompt to say which source person each picture replaces. Keep the existing prompt structure.
4. In Global Control, set mode, service URL, model, LoRA paths, width, height and fps.
5. Run and check the preview.

Case03: when changing source clips, update each segment's prompt, duration and guide/trim frames. Its current frame settings use 24 FPS.

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1>: The person defined by <Picture 1>, replacing the central performer originally wearing a pale suit in <Video 1>.
<Subject 2>: The person defined by <Picture 2>, replacing the right foreground person in <Video 1>.
<Subject 3>: The person defined by <Picture 3>, replacing the left background person in <Video 1>.
<Subject 4>: The person defined by <Picture 4>, replacing the left foreground person in <Video 1>.
<Subject 5>: The person defined by <Picture 5>, replacing the right background person in <Video 1>.
<Video 1>: The source performance, defining the original movements, expressions, interactions, visibility, camera, environment and timing.

summary:
Replace the five assigned source people with their respective picture identities, preserving the performance in <Video 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: attribute_transfer — appearance from <Picture 1>, source person's motion and expressions.
<Subject 2>: attribute_transfer — appearance from <Picture 2>, source person's motion and expressions.
<Subject 3>: attribute_transfer — appearance from <Picture 3>, source person's motion and expressions.
<Subject 4>: attribute_transfer — appearance from <Picture 4>, source person's motion and expressions.
<Subject 5>: attribute_transfer — appearance from <Picture 5>, source person's motion and expressions.
<Video 1>: partially_preserved — retain choreography, timing, camera, scene, lighting, interactions and visibility; replace only the assigned appearances.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] The source video alone defines the entire environment, background, lighting, camera, props and choreography. The reference pictures contribute only each assigned person's face, hair, clothing and worn accessories. Exclude the reference backgrounds, text, logos, presentation layouts, poses and handheld objects from the generated scene. Keep the source environment visible behind every replacement person throughout.

Each assigned identity belongs to exactly one source-person track. When a person leaves the view, their assigned identity leaves with them. The remaining central performer keeps <Picture 1> throughout; a departing person's appearance never transfers to that performer.

Reproduce the supplied source performance once in its original order and speed. Track each assigned source person continuously through movement, overlap and occlusion. Each person's face, hair, clothing and accessories match only that person's assigned picture throughout the shot. Preserve both the presence and absence of each appearance feature in that picture. Keep all five identities independent as the composition changes. Use all views of a reference as views of the same person. Render only the people visible in the source at each moment. Retain unassigned people, handheld props and the environment. Continuation guides establish the opening pose and composition; assigned pictures define appearance throughout. Preserve the existing source camera and shot boundaries.

overall_soundscape:
No additional dialogue or sound effects. Source soundtrack is restored during assembly.

non_diegetic_music:
No additional music.

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the target person in <Picture 1>, defining that person's face, hair, complete visible clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 6> is the central performer originally wearing a pale suit in <Video 1>, whose track is replaced by <Subject 1>.
<Subject 2> is the target person in <Picture 2>, defining that person's face, hair, complete visible clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 7> is the right foreground person in <Video 1>, whose track is replaced by <Subject 2>.
<Subject 3> is the target person in <Picture 3>, defining that person's face, hair, complete visible clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 8> is the left background person in <Video 1>, whose track is replaced by <Subject 3>.
<Subject 4> is the target person in <Picture 4>, defining that person's face, hair, complete visible clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 9> is the left foreground person in <Video 1>, whose track is replaced by <Subject 4>.
<Subject 5> is the target person in <Picture 5>, defining that person's face, hair, complete visible clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 10> is the right background person in <Video 1>, whose track is replaced by <Subject 5>.
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace each of <Subject 6> through <Subject 10> with the corresponding target <Subject 1> through <Subject 5>, preserving the source performance, scene, camera and timing.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - Preserve this person's face and all visible worn items from <Picture 1> throughout the source movement.
<Subject 6>: attribute_transfer - transfer only this source person's pose, actions, expressions, position and visibility to <Subject 1>; replace their face, hair, clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 2>: fully_preserved - Preserve this person's face and all visible worn items from <Picture 2> throughout the source movement.
<Subject 7>: attribute_transfer - transfer only this source person's pose, actions, expressions, position and visibility to <Subject 2>; replace their face, hair, clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 3>: fully_preserved - Preserve this person's face and all visible worn items from <Picture 3> throughout the source movement.
<Subject 8>: attribute_transfer - transfer only this source person's pose, actions, expressions, position and visibility to <Subject 3>; replace their face, hair, clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 4>: fully_preserved - Preserve this person's face and all visible worn items from <Picture 4> throughout the source movement.
<Subject 9>: attribute_transfer - transfer only this source person's pose, actions, expressions, position and visibility to <Subject 4>; replace their face, hair, clothing and worn accessories.
<Subject 5>: fully_preserved - Preserve this person's face and all visible worn items from <Picture 5> throughout the source movement.
<Subject 10>: attribute_transfer - transfer only this source person's pose, actions, expressions, position and visibility to <Subject 5>; replace their face, hair, clothing and worn accessories.
<Video 1>: partially_preserved - retain the source environment, lighting, camera, framing, choreography and timing; replace only the five assigned appearances.

detailed_description:
Preserve the source visual rendering, camera and lighting.
[Shot 1] The central source performer <Subject 6> is replaced by <Subject 1>. He sits on the bench and follows the cigarette-lighting performance, hand gestures and expressions in <Video 1>. The four surrounding source people are replaced separately: <Subject 7> by <Subject 2> at right foreground, <Subject 8> by <Subject 3> at left background, <Subject 9> by <Subject 4> at left foreground, and <Subject 10> by <Subject 5> at right background. Their hands interact with the central performer at the source positions. When the surrounding people rise, move apart and leave the frame, each assigned target follows only their own source track and leaves with that person. The central performer remains <Subject 1> as they lean forward, stand, turn and move across the stage following <Video 1>. At the end of this source action, the raised hand is empty and its bare index finger extends to point, following the exact hand shape, orientation and timing in <Video 1>. The earlier cigarette-lighting action ends at the source moment; objects remain only where and when they are actually visible in the source. Preserve this main person's target face, hair, clothing and worn accessories through the head and body turn. Keep each target's appearance separate during overlap and occlusion. Render only people visible in the source at each moment. Reference pictures supply appearance only; the environment, props, lighting, camera and action come from <Video 1>. Opening continuation guides establish the inherited pose and composition.

overall_soundscape:
No additional dialogue or sound effects. The original source soundtrack is restored during assembly.

No additional music.

nodes.title: Case03 · Multiple-Character Replacement Guide
widgets_values:
This case is tailored to the supplied 27-second video; it is not a general-purpose replacement workflow.

1. Replace the character images and each segment's source video.
2. Update each segment's prompt: B/C map five people; A/D/E replace only the central performer.
3. For a different video, recalculate segment durations, guide indices and trim/keep frames, and replace the assembly soundtrack. Current frame settings assume 24 FPS.
4. Check each segment preview before accepting the assembled result.
